sec: Pelvic brim, false/true pelvis & inlet diameters
q: Fill up: The true conjugate of the pelvic inlet runs from the sacral promontory to the ______ and measures about ______ cm.
opts: upper margin of the symphysis pubis; 11
lower margin of the symphysis pubis; 13
tip of the ischial spine; 11
tip of the coccyx; 9
exp: The true conjugate is the shortest antero-posterior diameter of the inlet and cannot be measured clinically, so the diagonal conjugate is used instead.

q: Match the pelvic plane with its description — 1) Plane of the inlet 2) Plane of greatest pelvic dimension 3) Plane of least pelvic dimension … A) Lies at the level of the ischial spines, with an antero-posterior diameter of about 11.5 cm B) A rounded inlet with a transverse diameter of about 13 cm C) The roomiest plane, with an antero-posterior diameter of about 12.75 cm
exp: The inlet is widest transversely, the mid-plane at the spines is the narrowest, and the plane of greatest dimension lies between them.

q: Fill up: The pelvic outlet has an antero-posterior diameter of about ______ cm and an intertuberous transverse diameter of about ______ cm.
exp: The outlet AP diameter runs from the lower border of the symphysis to the tip of the sacrum and the bituberous diameter between the ischial tuberosities.

sec: Significance of the ischial spine & stations
q: All of the following statements about the ischial spines are true EXCEPT:
opts: They are the landmark for the plane of the pelvic inlet
They mark the plane of least pelvic dimension
They are the reference point used to define fetal head station
They can be felt on vaginal examination lateral to the mid-line of the pelvis
exp: The ischial spines define the mid-pelvis and station zero, not the inlet, which is bounded by the sacral promontory and symphysis pubis.

q: A primigravida at term is fully dilated but the head shows no descent after two hours of good contractions, with increasing caput and moulding and three-fifths of the head still palpable abdominally. What is the diagnosis and management?
opts: Cephalopelvic disproportion — deliver by caesarean section
Normal progress — allow another two hours of pushing
Uterine inertia — start high-dose oxytocin augmentation
Deep transverse arrest — attempt manual rotation and forceps delivery
exp: Failure of descent after two hours of adequate contractions with caput and moulding means disproportion, not inertia, so oxytocin would be dangerous.

q: Match the Caldwell-Moloy pelvic type with its features — 1) Gynaecoid 2) Android 3) Anthropoid … A) A rounded or slightly oval inlet with a well-curved sacrum and roomy fore-pelvis, the favourable female pelvis B) A wedge-shaped inlet with convergent side walls, a narrow fore-pelvis and a shallow sacro-sciatic notch C) A long oval inlet with a generous antero-posterior diameter, favouring occipito-posterior positions
exp: Gynaecoid is favourable, android predisposes to deep transverse arrest, and anthropoid favours direct occipito-posterior delivery.
